content:
alice_support: FYI we have a customer (Acme) reporting missing audit events in their SIEM after enabling the S3 + syslog connector yesterday. They say gaps for ~45m starting 2026-02-18T03:12:00Z. They provided example event_ids that are present in live UI but absent from exported files.
acme_cs: Confirmed — we see the events in the Audit Viewer with IDs e7f3... and b1c9..., timestamps in that window, but the S3 prefix for that day only has batches up to sequence 12034 and then jumps to 12040.
alice_support: Customer is asking whether this is a retention/truncation bug or a forwarding delivery issue. Also mentioned seeing a few 403s from our SIEM forwarder in their logshipper. Attaching the snippet they sent:
logbot: ```
2026-02-18T03:15:02Z forwarder,error,upload failed, status=403, message="AccessDenied: kms:Decrypt denied for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-..."
2026-02-18T03:15:20Z forwarder,info,requeue batch id=12035
2026-02-18T03:16:01Z forwarder,error,upload failed, status=500, message="write timeout to s3://acme-audit/2026-02-18/part-12035"
```
ben_security: thanks, digging in. Initial hypotheses: 1) transient KMS permission errors causing forwarder to drop/rewrite batches, 2) exporter retry logic hitting a bug that marks batches as "skipped" when encountering mixed 4xx/5xx, 3) re-encryption/rotation job overlapping export window.
sam_infra: we rotated the export KMS key for S3 on 2026-02-18 at 03:10Z as part of scheduled rotation for customer keys (note: this key is customer-managed for Acme). There was a short period (~90s) where Decrypt calls failed until the new key alias propagated.
ben_security: that fits the 403s. But that shouldn't permanently drop events — the forwarder should retry. Can you check exporter's retry state and the DB flag for batches 12035-12039?
sam_infra: checking now.
sam_infra: quick snapshot from export_state table:
```
batch_id | status    | last_attempt_ts       | attempts
12033    | success   | 2026-02-18T03:09:58Z | 1
12034    | success   | 2026-02-18T03:11:40Z | 1
12035    | skipped   | 2026-02-18T03:15:22Z | 3
12036    | skipped   | 2026-02-18T03:15:39Z | 2
12037    | skipped   | 2026-02-18T03:15:55Z | 2
12038    | skipped   | 2026-02-18T03:16:12Z | 1
12039    | success   | 2026-02-18T03:17:05Z | 1
12040    | success   | 2026-02-18T03:18:01Z | 1
```
alice_support: interesting — 12035-12038 marked "skipped". Does our definition of skipped mean permanently dropped or just excluded from the current export window?
ben_security: "skipped" currently means exported process marked batch as non-retryable due to mixing client 4xx and server 5xx responses — that's a bug. It should become retryable on 5xx and only be dropped for immutable client errors. I'll open a quick fix to change classification logic.
kate_oncall: assigned. Also need mitigation for customer: can we re-export the missing range to their S3 prefix and resend syslog for those events? What's the best way to reconstruct without duplication risk?
sam_infra: we have raw audit journal stored (immutable) with sequence numbers. We can replay range 12035-12038 into a new batch id set with a forced reupload path. Two concerns: 1) if the customer already ingested partials, duplicates may occur, 2) syslog forwarder needs dedupe based on event_id, so safe if they dedupe.
ben_security: customer-side dedupe unknown. ask Acme to confirm. Meanwhile we should surface minimal repro steps and the patch to prevent recurrence.
alice_support: message to Acme: "We're investigating. Root cause looks like a KMS key rotation overlap that caused transient 403s and exposed a bug in our exporter retry classification which marked some batches as skipped. We can re-export the missing events if you want (will appear as new files). Please confirm if your SIEM dedupes by event_id; if not, we'll coordinate a maintenance window to ingest with de-duping off."
acme_cs: They replied: "We do not have dedupe in the SIEM. Please re-export but write to a separate prefix /replay/2026-02-18/ so we can test ingestion then delete. Also provide checksums and a list of event_ids so we can validate."
kate_oncall: plan:
1) short-term replay: replay batch_id range 12035-12038 to s3://acme-audit/replay/2026-02-18/ by EOD UTC. Provide manifest of event_ids + sha256 checksums.
2) patch: change exporter classification logic to treat 5xx as retryable + backfill any skipped batches automatically for 24h window.
3) postmortem and audit: add an alert when skipped-to-success ratio > 0.1 for any customer; update KMS rotation playbook to pause exports for 30s during alias propagation.
ben_security: I've opened PR #5487 with the retry fix and tests. Requesting code review from @sam_infra and @kate_oncall. Hotfix pipeline ready — we can deploy to exporters in us-east-1 staging then production.
sam_infra: started a one-off replay job. Command used:
```
redwood-auditctl replay --customer acme --from-seq 12035 --to-seq 12038 --target s3://acme-audit/replay/2026-02-18/ --manifest /tmp/acme-replay-manifest.json
```
logbot: ```
replay job submitted, job_id=rb-j-20260218-77
job status: running
estimated size: 12.4MB
```
alice_support: sending the customer a note that replay is running, will send manifest when done.
sam_infra: replay finished successfully. Manifest at /tmp/acme-replay-manifest.json, sample:
```
{
  "job_id": "rb-j-20260218-77",
  "from_seq": 12035,
  "to_seq": 12038,
  "files": [
    {"file": "part-12035-replay.gz", "sha256": "6b2f..."},
    {"file": "part-12036-replay.gz", "sha256": "c1a7..."}
  ],
  "event_ids": ["e7f3...","b1c9...","9d2a..."]
}
```
alice_support: sent manifest + S3 path to Acme. Also opened ticket to monitor for duplicates on their side during ingestion window.
acme_cs: They ack'd: "Received manifest and files under /replay/. Ingesting now, will confirm after validation. Thank you."
kate_oncall: follow-ups: 1) deploy PR #5487 to prod tomorrow 04:00Z, 2) add unit/integration test for mixed 403/500 sequences, 3) update KMS rotation doc to include 90s quiesce for exporter.
ben_security: noted. I'll draft the postmortem and link logs + metrics (exporter skipped batches, KMS rotation event, forwarder 403 spikes). Assigning to me for draft.
alice_support: closing customer loop once Acme confirms ingestion success. Will keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
logbot: ```
metrics: exporter.skipped_ratio[acme]=0.12 at 2026-02-18T03:17:00Z
alerts: none triggered
```
kate_oncall: also adding retention check: verify that skipped batches remain available for 30 days in journal. If not, we'll need to extend retention for affected customers.
sam_infra: retention for raw journal is 90 days for enterprise customers like Acme — safe.
alice_support: thread summary (to paste into ticket): "Missing audit events during 2026-02-18T03:12-03:17Z caused by customer KMS key rotation overlap + exporter retry classification bug. Replayed missing batches to s3://acme-audit/replay/2026-02-18/, manifest provided. Hotfix PR #5487 opened; deployment scheduled. Retention unaffected (90d). Postmortem in progress."
